A balloon... and your soul. A game of balance... and reflection.

Sometimes? Games don’t need a beginning and an end.

"We created a peaceful interactive experience that offers calming visuals and minimalistic gameplay. The game emphasizes the importance of the player’s thoughts and feelings as a big part of how the game is experienced. In that regard, we succeeded in our mission with C’est la balloon"

Made in Unity. I made all the art, and coded the game.

Our professor's favorite game was "Mountain." Yes, the game where you stare at a mountain. I found this to be funny, and decided to make him something that was right up his alley.

I did not make the audio effects or shaders for this game. 

Technically there was a team, but nobody actually did anything. I just did it all and assigned different aspects to different people so we would all get a good grade.

Dynamic third-person camera programmed in C# with Unity.

Able to perfectly stop camera clipping with only two raycasts.
Clean and readable initialization and update loop:
Here is the collision detection method:

The implementation uses layer masking to allow the designer to choose which objects the camera can or cannot collide with, so that detail elements of the scene do not cause poor camera behaviour.

The implementation uses a "nextCheck" value which allows the camera to reference from a single ray per-collision-- this both avoids stutter and allows for the system to function casting only one ray per frame under many conditions!

I created this asset for a game called Turtle Town, but it did not get used due to team dysfunction.

I sculpted and retopologized the turtle model in ZBrush, painted the textures in Substance Painter, and rigged it in Maya LT.

The screenshots you see are in Unity engine with orthographic projection, as was the intended display format for the game project.

The turtle is rendered using a stylized shader which gives an outline effect as well as quantized lighting bands. The shader was part of my art direction, but I did not code it.

The game's focus was to build a base on the back of a giant, living turtle. On the back of the turtle are stylized trees and monolithic rocks that jut from its shell.

The turtle is rigged to animate 3 tiers of progress for the player. Each town hall upgrade clears rocks and trees from the back of the turtle, openning up new areas for the player to expand their city:
